item.title: Breaking the Capacity‐Reversibility Linear Trade‐Off in Li–O 2 Batteries via Amorphous Non‐Precious High‐Entropy Alloy Catalysts
item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Amorphous non-precious MnFeCoNiCu high-entropy alloy catalyst breaks the capacity-reversibility trade-off in Li–O₂ batteries. Its porous structure promotes solution-mediated Li₂O₂ growth (10.8 mAh cm⁻²), while multielement electron redistribution lowers overpotential to 0.75 V and extends lifetime 4–5×. Scalable (>100 g) and viable in pouch cells (754 Wh kg⁻¹, 400 mA, −30°C), offering a cost-effective alternative to precious metals.
🏷 Li-O2 battery · high-entropy alloy · amorphous catalyst · capacity-reversibility trade-off · Li2O2 growth

item.title: Coupling Iodine Conversion and Zinc Ion Transport via Molecular Catalysis for Long‐Life Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Fe–TCPP porphyrin catalyst uniquely resolves the adsorption–transport conflict in Zn–I₂ batteries: its Fe–N₄ center moderately binds polyiodides (suppressing shuttling without passivation), while carboxyphenyl groups create a zincophilic microenvironment for Zn²⁺ access. This synchronized redox and ion regulation enables 50,000 cycles at 5 A g⁻¹ and stable pouch cells at 22 mg cm⁻² loading, establishing a molecular-catalytic design framework for aqueous batteries with soluble redox species.
🏷 zinc-iodine battery · molecular catalysis · polyiodide shuttling · porphyrin catalyst · long-life cycling

💡 MXene uniquely engineers Zn²⁺ transport, water structure, and interfacial reactions simultaneously, converting random deposition into uniform flux. This mechanistic integration of interface, architecture, and electrolyte design suppresses dendrites, hydrogen evolution, and corrosion, enabling stable, long-life aqueous zinc-ion battery anodes—advancing beyond single-factor approaches toward holistic anode stabilization.

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using a SnCl2 electrolyte additive to achieve coupled direct-contact presodiation and interphase stabilization of hard carbon anodes. This dual-function approach compensates for irreversible sodium loss during SEI formation, boosting initial coulombic efficiency while forming a stable interphase. It offers a simple, scalable strategy to overcome the low-ICE bottleneck limiting hard carbon anodes in sodium-ion batteries.
🏷 hard carbon · presodiation · SnCl2 additive · SEI stabilization · sodium-ion battery
